chunks: 5034 - And Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Abū Shibl, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A Muslim man committed fornication with the bondwoman of his brother; what is his repentance? He said:

"He should go to him, inform him, and ask him to make him lawful from that, and he must not return to it." I said: If he does not make him lawful regarding that? He said: "He will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as an adulterer and a betrayer."

He said: I said: Then is the Fire his destination? He said: "The intercession of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله and our intercession encompasses your sins, O community of the Shīʿah. So do not return, and do not rely upon our intercession. For by Allah, no one attains our intercession when he does this until the pain of punishment reaches him and he sees the terror of Jahannam."

key_terms.تَوْبَتُهُ: his repentance; the required turning back from the sin
key_terms.زَانِيًا خَائِنًا: as an adulterer and a betrayer; describing the gravity of the act
key_terms.شَفَاعَةُ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَي: the intercession of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.شَفَاعَتُنَا: the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: in a state of pardon or release from liability by the wronged person

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about repentance for zina involving another person’s rights and relying on shafa'ah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that repentance for violating another person’s right requires informing the wronged party, seeking his pardon, and not returning to the sin. It also warns that reliance on shafa'ah is not a license for wrongdoing, and that grave sins tied to betrayal and the rights of others carry painful consequences before relief comes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5034 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il through Salih ibn Uqbah from Abu Shibl who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a Muslim man who committed adultery with the bondwoman of his brother. What is his repentance?

Imam (as) replied: "He should go to him, inform him of what he has done, and ask him to pardon him, and he must not repeat the act."
I asked: "What if his brother does not pardon him?"
Imam (as) said: "Then he will meet Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, as an adulterer and a betrayer."

I asked: "Will Hellfire be his destination?"
Imam (as) replied: "The intercession of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and our intercession encompasses your sins, O' Shia community.
But do not return to such acts and do not rely on our intercession, for by Allah (swt), no one will attain our intercession if he commits this sin until he experiences the pain of punishment and witnesses the terror of Hell."
